description: The spawn-site gate fails at HEAD, red since 22-12 (ac4cd88): 6 offences, 5 'require with a non-literal specifier' in test/rails/probes/duplicateLoadProbe.cjs (lines 80, 102, 108, 133, 143) and 1 'call to exec()' in test/unit/guards/singleton.test.ts:66. 22-12's verification did not run this gate. Read in code, none is a spawn: the probe requires real project modules by computed path inside a railed child, and the exec call is a RegExp named RESULT_LINE that the receiver allow-list does not include. No child process and no production state is reached (22-13 wrapped runs: verdict untouched, nonLoopbackAllowed 0, telegramAllowed 0), so this is not a rail-class reach. The gate stays red until 22-15, whose first full-suite run will hit it. Likely fix: rename the receiver or add it to SAFE_EXEC_RECEIVERS, and add duplicateLoadProbe.cjs to ALLOWED_FILES with its reason. 22-13 does not fix it (Discovery rule); no 22-13 file is among the offences.
resolution: Fixed by the execute-phase orchestrator at the wave 9 boundary, commit f695363: test/rails/probes/duplicateLoadProbe.cjs is allowed a plain require of a computed path through COMPUTED_REQUIRE_FILES (all other gate checks still apply to it), and singleton.test.ts uses String.match instead of RegExp.exec. RED before the fix: the 6 offences. GREEN after: spawnSites and singleton tests, 34 passed, wrapped verdict untouched.

description: vi.doMock('../../src/db', ...) named a module that does not exist (the database module is src/utils/db.ts), so the mock was a silent no-op from the day the test was written (13-01, e0a0f0b). What the test actually exercised: the real src/utils/db module loaded and opened a real SQLite file when exitEngine was imported; its one assertion, buildExitConfig().stopLossPct === 18, reads CONFIG only and never touches the database, so the env -> CONFIG -> exitConfig claim was and is genuinely proven. Measured under the rails: with the broken specifier one run added 3 files to the per-worker temp test-DB folder (one DB plus its -wal and -shm); with the corrected specifier it added 0, and the same 10 tests pass both ways. No test passed only because of the no-op. The other 583 mock calls in the suite resolve. Historical note: before the 22-05 / 22-08 rails, this test opened whatever DB_PATH resolved to, with no src-layer tripwire; today resolveDbPath and assertNotProdDbUnderVitest keep it away from data/.
resolution: Specifier corrected with the smallest edit in the 22-14 Task 1 commit; recorded in rails-test-edits.json with register_as test-quality. 22-29 registers this as a test-quality finding.

description: The first full railed run shows this test is a live mainnet check sitting in the default integration suite: 'has bytecode at deployedAddress (not 0x)' calls provider.getCode() against process.env.ETH_RPC_URL and asserts the HoneypotChecker contract really has code on-chain. Under the rails ETH_RPC_URL is the sentinel http://127.0.0.1:1, so the call fails with ECONNREFUSED (fully wrapped runs vpu-20261109T042734-6628-578d1f and vpu-20261109T043212-18400-1f9f93; verdict untouched, net-watch 0 non-loopback). The test's guard is it.skipIf(!process.env.ETH_RPC_URL), which skipped it in CI but is false under a sentinel value, so the rails turned it from skipped into red. Before the rails this test made a real mainnet call whenever the operator's real .env set ETH_RPC_URL (AUD-TESTI-011). No bot code is at fault and no capital path is involved: preflight's checkHoneypotCheckerCode still does this getCode check against the real RPC at boot, src/preflight.ts:590,924. It cannot go green under the rails without a forbidden edit: a skip or sentinel-aware skip violates NAC-04 and the 0-skipped rule, deleting it violates P4, moving it out of the file breaks the same-file title identity rule, and a fake loopback RPC returning canned bytecode would mock the very thing it claims to check.
resolution: Operator ruling ESC-RAILS-01 (reply: b): the one test moved to the fork project in commit d66d8d0 (test/fork/honeypotDeploy.eth.fork.test.ts), assertions word for word. It has not run in its new file; the real run is obligation UFV-05, owner Phase 25. 22-29 registers this as a test-quality finding.
